The Thailand Relocation Guide

Eight ways to live in Thailand legally, priced from free to five million baht. Written the week five separate rules changed.

Edition v1.0.0 Verified September 8, 2026 Next review November 8, 2026 8 pathways 24 cited sources Navigator edition

Read this before you rely on anything here. This is researched reference material, not legal or tax advice, and no lawyer-client relationship is created by buying it. Immigration rules change without notice and are applied with discretion by individual officers. Every claim is numbered to a source you can check yourself, and each source is labelled with how much weight it carries.

Navigator edition. This guide was researched against public primary and government sources by its publisher. No licensed practitioner in Thailand has reviewed it, and we do not pretend otherwise. That is exactly why every pathway carries its own verify-this-yourself steps, naming the office that can answer, the question to ask, and what a real answer sounds like. Run them. They cost an hour and they are worth more than our assurance.

Everything here was verified on September 8, 2026. Before you spend money or book a flight, confirm the specific rule against the cited source or with a licensed Vietnamese immigration adviser. Baht figures assume roughly THB 32 to US$1. The rate moves; treat dollar conversions as order-of-magnitude. Note that Thai immigration and tax thresholds are set in baht, so a weakening dollar quietly raises the bar in dollar terms.

Start here: what is not true

Six beliefs that cost Americans the most money on the way to Thailand. We lead with these because the expensive mistakes happen before anyone files a form.

Widely believedAmericans get 60 days visa-free in Thailand.

Actually: Not from 15 September 2026. The regulation cutting visa-free entry from 60 days back to 30, for Americans and 59 other nationalities, was published on 31 August 2026 and applies to entries from 15 September. Anyone admitted before that date keeps the stay they were granted. The 60-day scheme ran from July 2024 and was always labelled exceptional. 91

Why the myth persists: Two years of blog posts, videos, and airline guidance say 60 days, and the change was published with fifteen days' notice. Almost nothing on the internet has caught up.

Widely believedThe DTV is Thailand's digital nomad visa, so it lets you live there.

Actually: It is a five-year multiple-entry visa, but each permitted stay is capped at 180 days, and — the part almost nobody mentions — it is legally classified as a Tourist visa under the Immigration Act. That classification is not academic: it is precisely why Thai banks now refuse DTV holders accounts, and why some accounts opened in 2024 are being frozen or closed. 1112

Why the myth persists: 'Five-year visa' is what the headline says. 'Five-year multiple-entry tourist visa with 180-day stays and no banking access' is what it is.

Widely believedYou can hop to Vientiane or Penang and pick up a DTV there.

Actually: Dead as of 31 August 2026. Applicants must now be a national or a permanent resident of the country where they apply. Being physically present in a third country is no longer enough. A criminal record clearance certificate is also now required. 10

Why the myth persists: The 'apply from a neighbouring country' route was the single most repeated piece of advice in the entire Thai nomad ecosystem for two years. Every guide, forum thread, and video recommending it is now wrong.

Widely believedThailand only taxes foreign income if you bring it in the same year you earned it.

Actually: That rule died on 1 January 2024. Under Departmental Instruction Por. 161/2566, foreign income earned from that date is taxable when a Thai tax resident remits it, regardless of which year it was earned. A 2025 proposal to exempt income remitted within two tax years was still not law as of mid-2026. Plan around the strict rule, not the relief. 2021

Why the myth persists: The old same-year rule was true for decades, and the proposed relief has been reported repeatedly as though it had passed.

Widely believedGet an education visa at a language school and you can stay indefinitely.

Actually: Roughly 10,000 student visas were revoked in 2026. Schools now report enrolment monthly into a centralised database that Immigration cross-checks continuously, officers make spot checks, and extension interviews can include being addressed in Thai to see whether you actually studied. This is a structural enforcement change, not a campaign. If you genuinely attend, you are fine. 18

Why the myth persists: The ED visa was a well-known workaround for fifteen years, and the schools selling it have every incentive not to mention the database.

Widely believedAn apostille will work for my US documents in Thailand.

Actually: Not yet. Thailand deposited its instrument of accession on 30 June 2026 and the Convention enters into force for Thailand on 28 February 2027. Until then the old consular legalization chain still applies. If you are comparing countries: Vietnam switched to apostilles on 11 September 2026, Cambodia has not joined at all, and Thailand switches next February. Three neighbours, three different answers, all in the same year. 22

Why the myth persists: Cabinet approval in December 2025 was widely reported as though the change had taken effect. Accession and entry into force are fourteen months apart.

Your pathway, in questions

Answer honestly rather than optimistically. Every answer narrows to exactly one route, including the routes that turn out not to exist. You can go back at any point.

    The pathways in full

    Every legal route, whether or not the tree sent you there. Read your own first, then read the one you would fall back to.

    Visa Exemption and Tourist E-Visa

    Exempt TR low

    The short-stay options, and the one changing in September 2026. Visa-exempt entry drops from 60 days to 30 for Americans on 15 September 2026; the 60-day tourist e-visa, extendable by 30 days, becomes the longer option.

    Best for
    Holidays, scouting trips, and the gap while a long-stay application is in progress.
    You get
    30 days visa-exempt from 15 September 2026, or 60 days on a tourist e-visa, extendable by 30 days at an immigration office
    Renewable
    Extensions are limited and discretionary. Repeated back-to-back entries attract questions at the border.
    Work locally
    No.
    Family
    Each traveller individually.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    Immediate on arrival, or a few business days for the e-visa.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    How many days you will actually be granted on arrival

    Ask: Thai Immigration Bureau, or the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington DC

    Ask, naming your nationality and your exact arrival date: 'As a US citizen arriving on [date], how many days of visa-exempt stay will I be granted?' www.immigration.go.th 9

    A real answer sounds like: A number of days tied to your date. If the answer is 60 and your arrival is on or after 15 September 2026, the person answering has not seen the 31 August regulation — ask again.

    That you are on the official e-visa portal and paying the official fee

    Ask: Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs

    Type the official portal address directly rather than arriving from a search result, and compare the checkout total against the published fee. www.thaievisa.go.th

    A real answer sounds like: A .go.th domain and a fee around US$40. Resellers charge two to three times this.

    Hard requirements

    • US passport valid at least 6 months 1
    • Thailand Digital Arrival Card completed before arrival — The TDAC replaced the paper arrival card. Complete it online in the days before you fly. 1
    • Onward ticket and proof of accommodation — Asked for inconsistently on visa-exempt entry and more often on repeat entries.

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Visa-exempt entryFree
    Tourist e-visaAbout US$40Confirm on the official Thai e-visa portal — never a reseller. 2
    30-day extension at an immigration officeTHB 1,900 1

    Step by step

    1. Check which rule applies to your arrival date

      Entries from 15 September 2026 get 30 days visa-exempt. Anyone admitted before that date keeps the 60 days they were granted. If your trip straddles the date, the date of entry is what counts. 9

      Who: You

    2. If you need more than 30 days, apply for the tourist e-visa before flying

      60 days, extendable by 30 at an immigration office for THB 1,900, giving 90 total. 2

      Who: You

    3. Complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card

      Online, before departure.

      Who: You

    4. Do not plan a life on repeated exempt entries

      Border officers see your entry history and repeated back-to-back exempt entries are the classic trigger for refusal.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Booking a 45-day trip on the assumption of 60 days visa-exempt

    Consequence: Overstay, at THB 500 per day, and a record that follows you.

    Avoid it: From 15 September 2026, budget 30 days or buy the tourist e-visa.

    Repeated exempt entries as a de facto residence strategy

    Consequence: Refusal of entry at the border, which is discretionary and not appealable in the moment.

    Avoid it: If you are living in Thailand, get a visa that says so.

    Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)

    DTV moderate

    Five years of multiple entries at 180 days a stay, for remote workers and for people doing qualifying Thai cultural activities. Genuinely useful, widely misunderstood, and materially harder to get than it was a month ago.

    Best for
    Remote workers under the LTR income threshold who can evidence THB 500,000 in savings, and people on genuine Muay Thai, Thai cooking, or medical programmes.
    You get
    5-year validity, multiple entry, 180 days per entry (one 180-day extension per entry is possible at an immigration office)
    Renewable
    The visa itself runs five years. Each stay is capped at 180 days and reset by leaving.
    Work locally
    No Thai employer, no Thai clients. It covers remote work for foreign employers and clients only.
    Family
    Yes — spouse and children under 20 apply in the Dependent category.
    Toward permanent residence
    No. It is classified as a Tourist visa.
    Realistic timeline
    Two to six weeks, plus however long your criminal record check takes. Apply well ahead of any travel.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    Whether your specific Thai mission is applying the 31 August rules, and what it accepts as proof of residence

    Ask: The Royal Thai Embassy or Consulate covering your US state

    Email asking: 'Under the rules effective 31 August 2026, what do you accept as evidence that I am a national or permanent resident of the United States, and what form of criminal record certificate do you require?' www.thaievisa.go.th 10

    A real answer sounds like: A named document list. Missions differ in practice, and the answer from the one handling your application is the only one that matters.

    Whether any Thai bank will open an account for a DTV holder right now

    Ask: The retail branches you would actually use, asked directly

    Before relying on Thai banking, email or visit two banks and ask: 'Do you currently open accounts for holders of the Destination Thailand Visa?' Ask a branch, not a call centre. 12

    A real answer sounds like: Probably no, or a request for documents you cannot produce. Enforcement varies by bank and branch, so a yes from one branch is not a policy.

    That your soft-power programme is on the qualifying list

    Ask: The Thai mission handling your application

    Send the institution's name and programme details and ask whether it qualifies before paying any tuition or deposit. 11

    A real answer sounds like: A yes or no naming the programme. General language schools have been excluded, so do not assume a language course qualifies.

    Hard requirements

    • THB 500,000 (about US$16,000) in a bank account, seasoned three months — It does not have to be a Thai account or in baht — a US account in dollars is accepted. It does have to have been sitting there for three months, and this is now strictly enforced. 1110
    • You must apply in a country where you are a national or a permanent resident — New from 31 August 2026. Being physically present in a third country is no longer sufficient. This closed the neighbouring-country application route entirely. 10
    • A criminal record clearance certificate — Also new from 31 August 2026. For Americans this is normally the FBI Identity History Summary. 10
    • Aged 20 or over, and physically outside Thailand when you apply 11
    • Category evidence — Workcation: an employment contract or certificate from a foreign employer, a letter confirming remote work and salary, and roughly six months of payslips or statements. Soft power: an acceptance letter from a registered Thai institution stating programme, duration, schedule and fee — note that general language schools are not on the qualifying list. Dependent: relationship documents. 11

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Application feeTHB 10,000 (about US$310) 11
    FBI Identity History Summary plus channelerUS$18 government fee, US$50 to 100 via an approved channeler
    180-day extension inside ThailandTHB 1,900 1

    Step by step

    1. Season the money first

      Three months in the account before you apply. If you have just moved the funds, wait — applying early is a wasted fee. 10

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Everything else waits on this.

    2. Order your FBI criminal record check

      Via an approved channeler for a days-long turnaround. 10

      Who: You

    3. Apply from the US, at a Thai mission covering your state

      You must apply where you are a national or permanent resident. Most missions now accept e-visa applications only. 102

      Who: You

    4. Plan your banking before you arrive, not after

      Assume you will not be able to open a Thai bank account on a DTV. Arrange US cards with no foreign transaction fee and a transfer service you trust. 12

      Who: You

    5. Track your 180-day clock from each entry

      Each entry starts a fresh 180 days. Leaving and returning resets it — and also triggers a fresh TM30 filing.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Applying from Laos, Vietnam, or Malaysia

    Consequence: Refused since 31 August 2026, and the THB 10,000 is gone.

    Avoid it: Apply in the US. The old advice is dead.

    Moving THB 500,000 into an account and applying the same week

    Consequence: Refused on seasoning.

    Avoid it: Three months, strictly enforced.

    Planning your finances around a Thai bank account

    Consequence: You arrive for a 180-day stay with no local banking and, increasingly, a frozen account if you had one.

    Avoid it: Treat Thai banking as unavailable on this visa and plan accordingly.

    Taking Thai clients or a Thai employer

    Consequence: That is work in Thailand without a work permit, on a visa classified as tourist.

    Avoid it: Foreign employers and foreign clients only. If you want to work locally, you want Non-B.

    Long-Term Resident Visa (LTR)

    LTR high

    Thailand's best long-stay product by a distance, and the most overlooked. Ten years, a digital work permit, exemption from the four-Thais-per-foreigner employment ratio, and — for three of its four categories — exemption from Thai tax on foreign income. Administered by the Board of Investment rather than Immigration.

    Best for
    Remote workers earning US$80,000+, retirees with US$80,000 of passive income, wealthy investors, and specialists in targeted industries.
    You get
    10 years, issued as 5 years renewable for a further 5
    Renewable
    Yes, on continuing qualification.
    Work locally
    Yes, via the digital work permit, and free of the standard 4:1 Thai-to-foreigner ratio.
    Family
    Yes — spouse and dependants are included, which is a major advantage over the DTV.
    Toward permanent residence
    Not directly, but it is the longest standard status Thailand issues.
    Realistic timeline
    Typically 8 to 20 weeks. The Board of Investment reviews qualification documents carefully and comes back with questions.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    Which category you actually qualify under, before you assemble evidence

    Ask: Thailand Board of Investment, LTR unit

    Use the BOI's own qualification enquiry with your real numbers, and ask which category they would assess you under and what evidence they require for it. ltr.boi.go.th 13

    A real answer sounds like: A named category and a document list. If you are told to just apply and see, ask again with specifics — the fee and the months are yours to lose.

    Whether the foreign-income tax exemption applies to your category and your income type

    Ask: Thai Revenue Department, and a Thai tax adviser

    Ask specifically whether the exemption covers your kind of income — employment, dividends, capital gains, pension — and get it in writing. Do not rely on a summary that says 'foreign income is exempt'. www.rd.go.th 20

    A real answer sounds like: An answer that distinguishes income types. This exemption is the main reason to choose LTR and is worth an hour of professional time to confirm.

    Hard requirements

    • Wealthy Global Citizen: US$1,000,000 in assets plus a US$500,000 investment in Thailand — The income test for this category was removed in February 2025. 134
    • Wealthy Pensioner: aged 50+, with US$80,000 a year in passive income — Or US$40,000 with additional investment conditions. 13
    • Work-from-Thailand Professional: US$80,000 a year from a well-established overseas employer, with 5+ years of relevant experience — Or US$40,000 with additional conditions. This is the category most high-earning remote workers should be looking at instead of the DTV. 13
    • Highly-Skilled Professional: working in a targeted industry for a Thai entity, institution, or government agency — This category carries a flat 17% personal income tax rate on Thai employment income instead of progressive rates to 35%. 13
    • Health insurance or evidenced medical cover — Requirements vary by category; confirm the current threshold with the Board of Investment.

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Visa feeTHB 50,000 (about US$1,560) for ten yearsRoughly US$156 a year — dramatically cheaper than Privilege and cheaper per year than annual retirement extensions once agent fees are counted.
    Digital work permitTHB 3,000 per yearOnly if you need to work.
    Qualifying investment, where the category requires oneUS$500,000 for Wealthy Global Citizen

    Step by step

    1. Identify your category before assembling anything

      The four categories have almost nothing in common in their evidence requirements. Applying under the wrong one wastes months. 134

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do this first.

    2. Assemble income or asset evidence in the form the BOI wants

      Employment contracts, tax returns, audited statements, and for the Wealthy Global Citizen category, asset valuations. This is a document exercise, not a form.

      Who: You Takes: Several weeks

    3. Apply online through the Board of Investment

      The LTR is not an Immigration Bureau product and does not go through a Thai embassy in the usual way. 4

      Who: You

    4. Collect the visa at a Thai mission or at an immigration office in Thailand

      Once endorsed by the BOI.

      Who: You

    5. Understand your tax position deliberately

      Three of the four categories carry an exemption from Thai tax on foreign income, which is the single largest financial difference between LTR and every other route in this guide. Get it confirmed in writing for your category. 1320

      Who: You and a Thai tax adviser

    How this goes wrong

    Defaulting to the DTV without checking LTR eligibility

    Consequence: You take a five-year tourist-classified visa with no banking and 180-day stays, when you qualified for ten years, a work permit, family inclusion, and a tax exemption for less money per year.

    Avoid it: If you earn US$80,000+, price the LTR before anything else. This is the most valuable single check in this guide.

    Applying under the wrong category

    Consequence: Months lost and a re-application.

    Avoid it: Confirm the category with the BOI before assembling evidence.

    Assuming the tax exemption is automatic and universal

    Consequence: A Thai tax assessment you did not budget for.

    Avoid it: Confirm in writing, by income type.

    Thailand Privilege (formerly Elite)

    PE low

    Buy your way past the paperwork. A one-time membership fee to a state-owned company, in exchange for a long-stay Privilege Entry visa with one-year stays, airport fast track, and a concierge who files your immigration paperwork for you. No income proof, no age limit, no financial disclosure.

    Best for
    People with money who value not dealing with immigration offices, and people who do not qualify for anything else but can afford to skip the question.
    You get
    5 to 20 years depending on tier, with one-year stays and multiple entry
    Renewable
    The membership runs its term; renewal means buying again.
    Work locally
    No. Privilege is not a work permit and does not entitle you to work in Thailand.
    Family
    Family members can be added at additional cost, depending on tier.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    Weeks. It is a purchase with background screening, not an application on merit.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    The current price and term of the tier you want, and whether Bronze is still available

    Ask: Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd., the state-owned operator

    Check prices on the official operator site rather than an agent's, and confirm the Bronze end date if that is the tier you want. thailandprivilege.co.th 14

    A real answer sounds like: A published fee and term. Agents sometimes quote outdated tiers or add fees to a product that has none.

    That the agent you are dealing with is authorised

    Ask: The official operator

    Ask the operator directly whether the agent is authorised before transferring a six-figure baht sum. thailandprivilege.co.th

    A real answer sounds like: Confirmation from the operator, not from the agent's own website.

    Hard requirements

    • The membership fee, and a clean background — There is no income test, no asset test, and no age requirement. That is the entire product. 14

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    BronzeTHB 650,000 (about US$20,300), 5 yearsScheduled to end on 30 September 2026 — if you want this tier, the window is closing. 14
    GoldTHB 900,000 (about US$28,100), 5 yearsAdds 20 service points a year. 14
    PlatinumTHB 1,500,000 (about US$46,900), 10 years 14
    DiamondTHB 2,500,000 (about US$78,100), 15 years 14
    ReserveTHB 5,000,000 (about US$156,000), 20 yearsInvitation only. 14

    Step by step

    1. Price it against the LTR first

      The LTR costs THB 50,000 for ten years. Privilege Platinum costs THB 1,500,000 for ten. If you qualify for LTR on income or assets, Privilege is thirty times the price for less — no work permit, no tax exemption, no family inclusion as standard. 1314

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do this comparison before paying anything.

    2. Apply through the official operator or an authorised agent

      Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd. is a state-owned enterprise. Verify any agent is authorised before transferring money. 1

      Who: You

    3. Pass background screening and pay the one-time fee

      There are no annual fees. 14

      Who: You

    4. Remember you still have Thai admin obligations

      Privilege members still file 90-day reports and TM30 notifications like everyone else. The concierge helps; the obligation is still yours. 191

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Buying Privilege when you qualified for LTR

    Consequence: Roughly thirty times the cost for a weaker product.

    Avoid it: Run the LTR check first. Always.

    Believing Privilege permits you to work

    Consequence: Working without a permit.

    Avoid it: It is a long-stay membership. Work requires Non-B and a work permit, or an LTR digital work permit.

    Paying an unauthorised agent

    Consequence: A very large, unrecoverable transfer.

    Avoid it: Verify with the operator first.

    Retirement: Non-O extension, O-A, and O-X

    Non-O O-A O-X moderate

    Three routes that look identical on money and differ enormously on insurance. Everyone calls them 'the retirement visa'; choosing between them is the most consequential decision a retiring American makes in Thailand.

    Best for
    Anyone 50 or over with THB 800,000 in a Thai bank or THB 65,000 a month in income.
    You get
    One year at a time for Non-O and O-A; O-X runs longer on much higher financials
    Renewable
    Yes, annually, indefinitely.
    Work locally
    No.
    Family
    A spouse can generally accompany on a dependent basis. Confirm for your circumstances.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    O-A: several weeks from the US. In-country Non-O conversion: a few weeks after arrival, plus a 30-day under-consideration period on the extension.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    Whether your local immigration office requires insurance on an in-country Non-O retirement extension

    Ask: The immigration office for the province you will live in

    Ask in person or by phone: 'For a one-year extension of stay based on retirement, applied for at this office on a Non-O, do you require health insurance?' Ask the office you will actually use — practice varies by province. www.immigration.go.th 15

    A real answer sounds like: A clear yes or no from that office. National rules and provincial practice are not always the same thing, and this office's answer is the one that governs you.

    The current bank deposit seasoning period and how it is measured

    Ask: The same immigration office

    Ask how many months the THB 800,000 must be in the account before applying, and how much must remain after the extension is granted. www.immigration.go.th

    A real answer sounds like: A number of months and a maintenance requirement. Getting this wrong is the most common cause of a refused retirement extension.

    That your insurer's policy is accepted, if you go the O-A route

    Ask: The Royal Thai Embassy handling your O-A application

    Send the policy schedule and ask whether it meets the US$100,000 requirement in the form they need it certified. 15

    A real answer sounds like: Acceptance of that specific policy. Do not buy insurance before asking.

    Hard requirements

    • Aged 50 or over 15
    • THB 800,000 in a Thai bank, or THB 65,000 a month in pension or income, or a combination totalling THB 800,000 a year — The same threshold applies across Non-O and O-A. Seasoning rules apply to the bank deposit — confirm the current period with your immigration office. 15
    • O-A only: health insurance of US$100,000 or THB 3,000,000 per policy year — Foreign insurance is accepted for the O-A. This requirement is the single biggest practical difference between the routes. 15
    • In-country Non-O extension: no legal insurance requirement — If you enter Thailand and convert to a Non-O, then extend annually inside the country, there is no insurance mandate. Many retirees do not know this route exists. 15
    • O-X: THB 3,000,000 fixed deposit, or THB 1,800,000 in Thailand plus THB 1,200,000 annual income, and Thai-issued insurance — Much higher financials and, unlike the O-A, foreign insurance is not accepted. 15

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Visa or extension feeTHB 1,900 to 5,000 depending on route 1
    Health insurance, O-AUS$1,500 to 6,000+ per yearRises steeply with age and pre-existing conditions. Price it before choosing the O-A.
    Re-entry permitTHB 1,000 single, THB 3,800 multipleEssential. See the gotcha — leaving without one cancels your extension. 1
    Agent assistance, optionalTHB 5,000 to 20,000 per year

    Step by step

    1. Choose your route on insurance, not on convenience

      If health insurance at US$100,000 cover is expensive or unobtainable for you — which becomes common past 70 or with pre-existing conditions — the in-country Non-O extension route avoids the mandate entirely. Work this out before you apply for anything. 15

      Who: You

      Blocked by: This decision is hard to reverse once you have entered on an O-A.

    2. If going the in-country route, enter and convert

      Enter Thailand, apply to convert to a Non-O, then apply for the one-year extension based on retirement.

      Who: You Where: Thai immigration office

    3. Open a Thai bank account and season the deposit

      The THB 800,000 route requires the money in a Thai account in your name for a set period before applying. Retirement-class visas do open accounts, unlike the DTV. 12

      Who: You

    4. Buy a re-entry permit before any trip abroad

      Without one, leaving Thailand cancels your extension of stay outright. 1

      Who: You

    5. Set up your 90-day reporting routine

      Every 90 consecutive days in Thailand, for as long as you live there. 19

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Applying for the O-A from the US without pricing the insurance

    Consequence: You are locked into an annual insurance mandate that can cost thousands and becomes harder to satisfy with age.

    Avoid it: Price it first, and compare against the in-country Non-O route which has no mandate.

    Leaving Thailand without a re-entry permit

    Consequence: Your extension of stay is cancelled. You return as a tourist and start again.

    Avoid it: Buy the multiple re-entry permit at the same time as the extension.

    Dropping the bank balance after the extension is granted

    Consequence: Refusal at the next renewal, when the officer reviews the year's statements.

    Avoid it: Understand the maintenance requirement, not just the application-day figure.

    Non-Immigrant B and Work Permit

    Non-B high

    The employment route. Two documents again: the Non-B visa to enter and stay, and a work permit from the Department of Employment to work. The binding constraint is not you — it is whether your employer is large enough to be allowed to hire you.

    Best for
    Anyone with a Thai employer of real size: multinationals, established Thai companies, international schools.
    You get
    Non-B for 90 days initially, then one-year extensions of stay tied to the work permit
    Renewable
    Yes, annually, while employed.
    Work locally
    Yes, for the sponsoring employer, in the permitted role.
    Family
    Yes, dependants on Non-O.
    Toward permanent residence
    It is the only route that realistically leads there, after at least three consecutive years of extensions with matching tax filings — against a quota of roughly 100 per nationality per year.
    Realistic timeline
    6 to 12 weeks, dominated by employer documentation and US document legalization.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    That your prospective employer meets the 4:1 ratio and the capital requirement

    Ask: The employer's HR, and the Department of Employment

    Ask HR for the current Thai headcount, foreign headcount, and registered capital, and ask how many work permits they have obtained in the past year. www.doe.go.th 16

    A real answer sounds like: Three numbers and a track record. A company that has never obtained a work permit before is a serious risk, however good the job is.

    That your job title is not on the restricted occupations list

    Ask: Department of Employment

    Give the exact title that will appear on the permit application and ask whether it is permitted for a foreign national. www.doe.go.th 16

    A real answer sounds like: A clear yes or no against that title. Titles matter more than duties here.

    Which document authentication your employer needs, given the February 2027 switch

    Ask: The employer, and the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington DC

    Ask whether they need consular legalization now or can wait for apostille acceptance from 28 February 2027. 22

    A real answer sounds like: A clear instruction tied to the filing date. If your filing is close to the switch, the timing is worth planning.

    Hard requirements

    • Your employer must maintain a 4:1 ratio of Thai to foreign employees — Four Thai employees for every foreign one. This is the constraint that rules out small companies and startups entirely. 16
    • Your employer must hold registered capital of THB 2,000,000 per foreign worker — Some sources cite THB 2 to 3 million. Two foreign staff means at least THB 4,000,000 of registered capital. 16
    • The role must not be on the Ministry of Labour's restricted occupations list — A list of professions reserved for Thai nationals. Check it against your actual job title. 16
    • Degree and supporting documents, legalized — Until 28 February 2027 this means consular legalization, not an apostille. 22

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Non-B visaAbout US$80 to 200 depending on entries 2
    Work permitTHB 3,000 to 6,000 per yearUsually paid by the employer. 3
    One-year extension of stayTHB 1,900 1
    US document legalizationUS$200 to 600Falls once the apostille takes effect on 28 February 2027. 22

    Step by step

    1. Before accepting the offer, ask the ratio and capital questions

      Ask HR directly: how many Thai employees does the entity have, how many foreign staff, and what is its registered capital? If the arithmetic fails, no permit can be issued regardless of your qualifications. 16

      Who: You

      Blocked by: This is the whole gate.

    2. Employer obtains the WP.32 pre-approval

      Filed with the Labour Department before you apply for the visa. 16

      Who: Your employer

    3. Legalize your degree and supporting documents

      Consular legalization until 28 February 2027, when apostilles take over. 22

      Who: You Takes: 4 to 8 weeks

    4. Apply for the Non-B at a Thai mission in the US

      Applied for at the Thai mission covering your state, with the WP.32 pre-approval and employer documents. Most missions accept e-visa applications only.

      Who: You

    5. Enter, obtain the work permit, then extend the stay to one year

      The extension is granted on the strength of the work permit and employer documents.

      Who: You and your employer

    6. Set up TM30, 90-day reporting, and a re-entry permit

      All three apply from the moment you have a long stay. 19

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Joining a small company or startup

    Consequence: The 4:1 ratio and capital requirement cannot be met, and no permit can be issued.

    Avoid it: Ask the numbers before you resign from anything.

    Working before the permit is issued

    Consequence: Illegal employment, with exposure for you and your employer.

    Avoid it: No work — including remote work for the Thai entity — before the permit exists.

    Assuming the permit and visa move with you to a new job

    Consequence: Neither does. Both are employer-specific.

    Avoid it: Never resign before the new employer's filing is underway.

    Marriage Visa (Non-O, spouse of a Thai national)

    Non-O moderate

    The cheapest durable route into Thailand, at half the financial threshold of retirement and with no age requirement. Annual extensions, sometimes with a home visit.

    Best for
    Foreign spouses of Thai citizens.
    You get
    Enter on a 90-day Non-O, then one-year extensions inside Thailand
    Renewable
    Yes, annually, while married.
    Work locally
    The marriage extension is not a work permit, but it does support obtaining one on easier terms than Non-B. Confirm for your situation.
    Family
    Children of the marriage are covered on a family basis.
    Toward permanent residence
    Marriage is one of the categories under which permanent residency can eventually be sought. Treat it as a long-horizon possibility, not a plan.
    Realistic timeline
    Two to four months including the 30-day under-consideration period on the extension.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    What your local immigration office requires to recognise a US marriage

    Ask: The immigration office and the district office (amphur) where your spouse is registered

    Ask what form of certification and translation of a US marriage certificate they accept, and whether the marriage must be re-registered at the amphur. www.immigration.go.th 17

    A real answer sounds like: A named process. Provincial practice varies more on this than on almost anything else in Thai immigration.

    The seasoning period and whose name the account must be in

    Ask: The same immigration office

    Ask how long the THB 400,000 must be in the account, and confirm it must be a sole account in your name. www.immigration.go.th

    A real answer sounds like: A number of months and a clear statement about account ownership.

    Hard requirements

    • THB 400,000 in a Thai bank in your name for two months before applying, or THB 40,000 a month in income — Half the retirement threshold. Confirm the seasoning period with your local office. 17
    • A marriage registered at a Thai district office, or registered abroad and recognised — A US marriage must be certified, translated, and recognised by Thai authorities. 17
    • Your Thai spouse attends the appointment — Offices expect it, and their absence is a common cause of a wasted trip. 17

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Non-O visa and one-year extensionTHB 2,000 to 5,000 1
    Document certification and translationUS$200 to 500
    Re-entry permitTHB 1,000 single, THB 3,800 multiple 1

    Step by step

    1. Get the marriage recognised Thai-side

      If you married in the US, this gates everything else. Certification, translation, and recognition. 17

      Who: You and your spouse

      Blocked by: Nothing proceeds without it.

    2. Enter on a Non-O based on marriage

      Applied for at a Thai mission, or converted in-country from a qualifying entry.

      Who: You

    3. Season THB 400,000 in a Thai account in your own name

      Two months before applying for the extension. The account must be yours, not joint and not your spouse's. 17

      Who: You

    4. Apply for the one-year extension with your spouse present

      Expect a roughly 30-day under-consideration stamp, and possibly a home visit or a call to your spouse before the full year is granted. 17

      Who: You and your spouse

    5. Buy a re-entry permit, and set up TM30 and 90-day reporting

      The re-entry permit protects the extension you just spent months obtaining; the reporting obligations start immediately and run for as long as you live there. 19

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Holding the money in a joint account or your spouse's account

    Consequence: Refused.

    Avoid it: Sole account, your name.

    Attending the extension appointment without your spouse

    Consequence: A wasted trip, and sometimes a wasted month.

    Avoid it: Bring them.

    Leaving Thailand during the 30-day under-consideration period without checking

    Consequence: Complications with the pending extension.

    Avoid it: Ask the office before booking travel.

    Education Visa (ED)

    ED moderate

    Legitimate if you genuinely study, and a closing door if you do not. Roughly 10,000 student visas were revoked in 2026 as enforcement moved to continuous database cross-checking.

    Best for
    People actually enrolling in a Thai university, or genuinely committing to learning Thai at an accredited school.
    You get
    Tied to the programme, extended in blocks
    Renewable
    Yes while genuinely enrolled and attending. After about a year you are generally expected to progress to a different course or level.
    Work locally
    No.
    Family
    Limited. Do not plan a family move around this.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    4 to 10 weeks from enrolment.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    That the school is currently approved and its students' visas are not at risk

    Ask: Thai Immigration Bureau, and the school

    Ask the school how many ED visas they supported last year, whether any of their students were affected by the 2026 revocations, and ask to speak to a current student. Then confirm the school's standing with immigration. www.immigration.go.th 18

    A real answer sounds like: Numbers and a student contact. Evasiveness about the 2026 revocations is the answer.

    What attendance level is actually required to keep the visa

    Ask: The school and your local immigration office

    Ask for the attendance percentage they report and what happens at the extension interview.

    A real answer sounds like: A specific percentage and a description of the interview. 'Don't worry about it' means you are buying a visa, not a course — which is exactly what was revoked at scale.

    Hard requirements

    • Enrolment at an institution approved by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation — Schools now report enrolment monthly into a centralised database that Immigration cross-checks. 18
    • Genuine attendance — Not a formality. Officers make spot checks, extension interviews can include being addressed in Thai, and students who skip class are refused extensions. 18

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Thai language course, one yearTHB 25,000 to 60,000 (about US$780 to 1,900)
    Visa and extensionsTHB 2,000 to 5,000 per year 1

    Step by step

    1. Verify the school is accredited and currently in good standing

      Schools that lose their licence take their students' visas with them. This happened at scale in 2026. 18

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do this before paying tuition.

    2. Enrol and obtain the school's visa support documents

      The school issues the visa support letter and is recorded as your sponsor in the centralised database that Immigration cross-checks.

      Who: You and the school

    3. Apply for the ED visa

      At the Thai mission covering your state, with the school’s support documents.

      Who: You

    4. Actually attend

      Attendance is reported monthly and cross-checked. This is the whole compliance model now. 18

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Buying an ED visa from a school as a stay-in-Thailand product

    Consequence: This is precisely what the 2026 revocations targeted. Roughly 10,000 visas were cancelled.

    Avoid it: If you are not going to attend, choose a different route.

    Paying a year of tuition before checking the school's standing

    Consequence: The school loses its licence and your visa support disappears with your money.

    Avoid it: Verify first, pay second.

    Ten traps

    Cross-cutting failures that belong to no single pathway. If you read only one section of this guide, read this one.

    1Visa-free entry drops to 30 days on 15 September 2026

    trip ending

    The trap. The regulation cutting visa-exempt stay from 60 days to 30 for Americans and 59 other nationalities was published on 31 August 2026 and applies to entries from 15 September. Anyone admitted before that date keeps what they were granted. Two years of guides, videos, and airline pages still say 60.

    Do this instead. If you arrive on or after 15 September 2026, budget 30 days, or buy the 60-day tourist e-visa before flying and extend it by 30 at an immigration office for THB 1,900. 9

    Tied to a rule change — re-check this after December 15, 2026.

    2The DTV is legally a tourist visa, and Thai banks now act on that

    expensive

    The trap. The DTV is classified as Tourist under the Immigration Act. Since 2026, major Thai banks have refused new accounts to tourist-classified visa holders, and some accounts opened in 2024 have been frozen or closed on compliance review. Enforcement varies by bank and branch, which is why the forums disagree.

    Do this instead. Plan on having no Thai bank account on a DTV. If Thai banking matters, that is a reason to price the LTR or a Non-Immigrant route instead — make it part of the pathway choice, not a discovery after you arrive. 12

    3You can no longer get a DTV from a neighbouring country

    expensive

    The trap. From 31 August 2026, applicants must be a national or a permanent resident of the country where they apply. The Vientiane and Penang runs that dominated two years of advice are finished. A criminal record certificate is now required as well.

    Do this instead. Apply in the United States, at the mission covering your state, and order your FBI Identity History Summary before you start. 10

    4TM30 must be re-filed after every single re-entry

    annoying

    The trap. The address notification is due within 24 hours of arriving at a residence — and a new one is required every time you re-enter Thailand, even returning to the exact same apartment you left. A weekend trip to Singapore restarts the clock. The duty sits with the property owner, so tenants assume it is handled and it often is not.

    Do this instead. Agree with your landlord at the start who files it and how, and get confirmation each time. Keep every receipt — a missing TM30 surfaces at your next extension appointment. 19

    5Leaving Thailand without a re-entry permit cancels your extension

    trip ending

    The trap. An extension of stay is not a multiple-entry visa. Exit the country without a re-entry permit and the extension you spent months and money obtaining is void. You return as a tourist and start over.

    Do this instead. Buy the multiple re-entry permit at THB 3,800 at the same time as your extension, every year, without thinking about it. 1

    690-day reporting applies to you, whatever you paid

    annoying

    The trap. Every foreigner present more than 90 consecutive days must report, including Privilege members who assumed the concierge fee bought them out of it. The counter resets on re-entry. And if you have left Thailand since your last report, the online system will not accept you — you must file in person.

    Do this instead. Diarise it from your entry stamp, file online when eligible, and expect to go in person after any trip abroad. The fine is THB 2,000, or THB 5,000 if you are caught rather than volunteering. 19

    7The same-year remittance rule died in 2024, and the relief never passed

    expensive

    The trap. For decades, foreign income was only taxable if remitted in the year it was earned. Departmental Instruction Por. 161/2566 ended that for income earned from 1 January 2024 — now it is taxable whenever a tax resident brings it in. A 2025 proposal for a two-year exemption window has been widely reported as though it passed. As of mid-2026 it is not law.

    Do this instead. Plan around the strict rule. If you are moving a large sum, get advice on timing relative to your Thai tax residency before you transfer, not after. 2021

    8The DTV's THB 500,000 must have been sitting there three months

    expensive

    The trap. The money need not be in Thailand or in baht — a US dollar account counts — but the three-month seasoning is now strictly enforced. Applicants who move funds and apply the same week are refused, and the THB 10,000 fee is not refundable.

    Do this instead. Get the balance in place, then wait three months, then apply. If you are close, waiting is free and refusal is not. 1011

    9The retirement route you pick decides whether insurance is mandatory

    expensive

    The trap. The O-A, applied for from the US, requires health insurance of US$100,000 or THB 3,000,000 per policy year. The in-country Non-O extension has no legal insurance requirement at all. Most guides describe both as 'the retirement visa' and never mention the difference, which is worth thousands a year and becomes decisive with age or pre-existing conditions.

    Do this instead. Get an insurance quote at your actual age before choosing. If it is expensive or you are declined, enter Thailand and convert to a Non-O in-country instead, then extend annually. 15

    10Thailand Privilege Bronze ends on 30 September 2026

    annoying

    The trap. The cheapest tier at THB 650,000 for five years is scheduled to close. Agents will keep advertising it after it goes.

    Do this instead. If Bronze is the tier you want, confirm availability directly with the state-owned operator, not with an agent. And run the LTR comparison first — it may make the question moot. 14

    Tied to a rule change — re-check this after November 1, 2026.

    11Apostilles do not work in Thailand until 28 February 2027

    expensive

    The trap. Thailand's cabinet approved accession in December 2025 and the instrument was deposited on 30 June 2026, but entry into force is 28 February 2027. Until then the consular legalization chain still applies. The December announcement was widely reported as though the change was live.

    Do this instead. Use consular legalization now: state certification where applicable, US Department of State authentication, then Royal Thai Embassy legalization. If comparing the region — Vietnam accepts apostilles from 11 September 2026, Cambodia has not joined at all, Thailand joins in February 2027. Three neighbours, three different answers. 22

    Tied to a rule change — re-check this after April 1, 2027.

    12Buying Privilege when you qualified for LTR costs about thirty times more

    expensive

    The trap. Thailand Privilege Platinum is THB 1,500,000 for ten years. The LTR is THB 50,000 for ten years and adds a digital work permit, family inclusion, exemption from the 4:1 employment ratio, and — for three of its four categories — exemption from Thai tax on foreign income. Privilege is sold hard by agents on commission; the LTR is administered by the Board of Investment and sold by nobody.

    Do this instead. Check LTR eligibility before you consider Privilege. If you earn US$80,000, hold US$1,000,000 in assets, or are 50+ with US$80,000 of passive income, you are probably in LTR territory. 1314

    Where the sources disagree

    Questions credible sources answer differently. We publish the disagreement rather than picking a side and hoping — a guide that hides a genuine conflict is more dangerous than one that names it.

    Can a DTV holder open a Thai bank account?

    Position 1

    No, in practice. The DTV is classified as Tourist under the Immigration Act, banks have tightened enforcement against tourist-classified visas since 2026, and existing accounts are being frozen or closed on review. 12

    Held by: Banking and immigration practitioners reporting through 2026

    Position 2

    Sometimes, depending on the bank and the branch. Enforcement is inconsistent, and holders continue to report successful openings, particularly with a Thai address, a long lease, and an introduction. 12

    Held by: Ongoing expat community reports

    What this actually means for you. Both are true, which is why the forums look contradictory. A success at one branch is not a policy, and an account opened today can be closed at the next compliance review. The planning question is not whether it is possible but whether you can afford to be wrong.

    How to settle it for your own case. Do not resolve it — design around it. Assume no Thai banking on a DTV, and if that is unacceptable, choose LTR or a Non-Immigrant route instead. If you want to try anyway, ask two branches directly before you rely on it. 1211

    Is Thailand about to tax worldwide income, or relax the remittance rule?

    Position 1

    Relief is coming. A 2025 Revenue Department draft would exempt foreign income remitted within two tax years of being earned, which would substantially soften Por. 161. 20

    Held by: Widely reported since mid-2025

    Position 2

    Tightening is coming. A separate proposal would move Thailand to taxing residents on worldwide income regardless of remittance, which would be a far bigger change in the opposite direction. 2021

    Held by: Also reported, less widely

    What this actually means for you. Neither has been enacted. Two contradictory proposals are circulating and both are regularly described as though they had passed. The only safe planning basis is the rule actually in force: foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 is taxable when a tax resident remits it.

    How to settle it for your own case. Plan on the current rule and treat either change as a reason to revisit, not a reason to wait. If you hold or expect an LTR in one of the three exempt categories, get the exemption's scope confirmed in writing for your income type — that is a stronger position than any proposal. 2021

    Does the in-country Non-O retirement extension really have no insurance requirement?

    Position 1

    Correct, there is no legal insurance requirement for a retirement extension applied for inside Thailand on a Non-O. The mandate attaches to the O-A and, in a stricter Thai-issued form, to the O-X. 15

    Held by: The prevailing reading of the rules

    Position 2

    In practice it depends on your province. Immigration offices apply discretion, some ask for insurance regardless, and requirements have been known to differ between offices in the same year.

    Held by: Reports from applicants across different provinces

    What this actually means for you. The national rule and your local office's practice are not the same thing, and it is your local office that decides. This is the single most consequential provincial variation in Thai immigration.

    How to settle it for your own case. Ask the immigration office for the province you will actually live in, before you commit to a location. The answer from Chiang Mai does not bind Jomtien, and vice versa. 151

    The move itself, phase by phase

    Eight phases, in order. These apply whichever pathway you took; items marked with a pathway only appear for that route. Your ticks are saved in this browser.

    DecideDocumentsLeave United StatesMoneyArrivalFirst 90 daysOngoingContingency

    Decide and pressure-test

    T-120 to T-60 days

    Thailand has eight products at wildly different prices. Ten minutes of comparison here is worth more than anything else in this guide.

    Assemble and legalize documents

    T-120 to T-45 days

    Thailand switches to apostilles on 28 February 2027. Until then, the old chain applies — and getting this backwards costs weeks.

    Close out the United States

    T-90 to T-0 days

    Standard US departure admin, with one Thailand-specific difference worth checking yourself.

    Money and banking

    T-60 to T+60 days

    In Thailand your visa class determines your banking access. This is new, it is enforced, and it should influence which pathway you choose.

    Arrival week

    T-0 to T+7 days

    One 24-hour deadline, and one clock that starts the moment you are stamped in.

    First 90 days

    T+7 to T+90 days

    Converting arrival into a stable status, and setting up the admin rhythm you will keep for years.

    Staying legal, year after year

    Continuous

    Thailand has more recurring obligations than either Vietnam or Cambodia. Build the calendar once and it becomes routine; ignore it and it compounds.

    Contingency and exit

    Have this before you need it

    Written while things are going well.

    What we are watching

    Rules that are moving, or expected to. Each carries the date we next check it. When one lands, this guide is updated and you get the new edition — that is what your purchase actually buys beyond the first read.

    Visa-exempt stay cut from 60 days to 30

    Passed, not yet in force Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by September 20, 2026

    Once in force, the reality-check entry and the short-stay pathway both simplify to a plain 30-day statement, and the transition warning can be retired. 9

    Affects: Visa Exemption and Tourist E-Visa

    Apostille Convention enters into force for Thailand

    Passed, not yet in force Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by January 15, 2027

    The entire documents module switches from consular legalization to a single apostille, cutting cost and weeks from the work permit pathway. Existing Contracting States had until around 30 December 2026 to object. 22

    Affects: Non-Immigrant B and Work Permit, Marriage Visa (Non-O, spouse of a Thai national), Education Visa (ED)

    Two contradictory foreign-income tax proposals

    Proposed only Impact if it lands: pathway changing We re-check by December 1, 2026

    One proposal would exempt income remitted within two tax years; another would move Thailand to worldwide taxation regardless of remittance. Either would require rewriting the money and ongoing modules, in opposite directions. 2021

    Bank enforcement against tourist-classified visas

    Enforcement shifting Impact if it lands: pathway changing We re-check by November 15, 2026

    If banks extend or relax the tourist-class exclusion, the DTV's practical value changes substantially, as does the case for choosing LTR over it. 12

    Affects: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)

    Education visa enforcement via the centralised database

    Enforcement shifting Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by December 1, 2026

    Roughly 10,000 student visas were revoked in 2026 and the database now runs continuously. Further tightening would move the ED pathway toward a dead end for anyone not genuinely studying. 18

    Affects: Education Visa (ED)

    Thailand Privilege Bronze tier closing

    Passed, not yet in force Impact if it lands: minor We re-check by October 5, 2026

    The cheapest Privilege tier disappears from the cost table, raising the effective entry price of the pathway to THB 900,000. 14

    Affects: Thailand Privilege (formerly Elite)

    Proposed increase of the condominium foreign quota to 75%

    Proposed only Impact if it lands: minor We re-check by February 1, 2027

    Would ease condo purchases in buildings currently at their 49% cap. None of the proposed quota or leasehold reforms had been enacted as of 2026. 23
